Latin word

ōrātiō

ōrātiō, ōrātiōnis f.

noun, third declension · Declension on Wiktionary

a main clause; a prayer; prayer; a speech; speech, the power of speaking; a way of speaking

In this lexicon

  • clause

    also used · modern · Traupman 292

  • prayer

    also used · late Latin · Vulg. Act. 1.14: erant persevērantēs ūnanimiter in ōrātiōne; Vulg. Jac. 5.15

  • speech

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Brut. 91: scrībuntur ōrātiōnēs habitae jam; Traupman 176: ōrātiōnem habēre, give a speech; Traupman 302: (ōrātiōnem) habēre

  • speech

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Off. 1.50: ejus autem vinculum est ratiō et ōrātiō; Cic. Off. 1.12: ad ōrātiōnis et ad vītae societātem

  • ōrātiō solūta: prose

    classical

Examples

  • et ōrātiō fideī salvābit īnfirmum

    and the prayer of faith will save the sick manVulg. Jac. 5.15

    In the entry for prayer

  • sed quid agō? paene ōrātiōnem in epistulam inclūsī.

    But what am I doing? I’ve nearly put a whole speech into a letter.Cic. Att. 1.16.10

    In the entry for speech

  • plēraeque enim scrībuntur ōrātiōnēs habitae jam, nōn ut habeantur

    for most speeches are written down once they have been given, not in order to be givenCic. Brut. 91

    In the entry for speech

  • ōrātiōnem habēre

    to make a speechTraupman 383

    and its bond is reason and speech, which by teaching, learning, sharing, debating and judging bring people together and join them in a kind of natural fellowshipCic. Off. 1.50
